$comment: Conformance vectors for SPEC §2 — the normative derivation of axes.reversibility.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. reversibility is a hard precondition of BOTH rules that
hold a destructive action: R2 (irreversible + broad + production ->
require_approval) and R3 (irreversible + systemic + production -> deny). No other
rule in the shipped pack reads the axis. So a single wrong `recoverable` disables
the two rules the product is sold on, silently, for that action — and until this
file existed there was no suite for the axis. SPEC §7 has always said an adapter
'MUST pass the conformance suite' for the axes; for this one there was nothing to
pass. Sibling of blast-radius.json (RFX-131), same reason, same shape.
THE GROUND TRUTH RULE. `recoverable` means the SYSTEM BEING ACTED ON retains
something a human can restore from after the call returns. It is a property of
the object kind, not of the verb. The WordPress reference adapter used to answer
`recoverable` for every small delete on the strength of a 'WP trash default':
that default is real for post-type objects and comments and does not exist for
users, terms, options, meta, plugins, themes or tables. wp_delete_user() has no
trash to go to.
TWO CROSS-CUTTING RULES, both stated as cases below:
1. Spending the undo is not recoverable. `core/empty-trash` IS the restore
capability being consumed; it can never itself be `recoverable`.
2. An action cannot be both site-wide and undoable. Where an adapter prices
blast_radius `broad` or `systemic`, `recoverable` contradicts it inside one
envelope, and the honest answer is `irreversible`.
HOW A CASE IS WRITTEN. `given` states the situation ABSTRACTLY — what the adapter
knows about the object kind and the undo available to it at the call site — so the
case is the same case in every language. `bindings` then gives the concrete call
for each adapter that implements it.
ADAPTER STATUS AT THE TIME THIS FILE LANDED (measured, qa--023). The WordPress
reference adapter passes all of these; reeflex-wordpress/tests/
conformance-reversibility.php runs the file, in the gate. The Claude Code reference
adapter is NOT yet wired to it and does not pass: measured cross-adapter, the two
reference adapters disagree on 5 of 6 comparable operations, because
reeflex-claude answers `irreversible` for every shell removal while
reeflex-wordpress answered `recoverable` for every ability-level deletion. Some of
those rows are additionally distorted by RFX-144 (classify.py::_bash_verb reads
only the first shell token, so `wp user delete ...` is not seen as a delete at
all). Wiring the Claude Code runner is deliberately left to the RFX-144 fix so
the two changes do not collide — see the ticket filed with this file.

The binding is deliberately PREDICATE-shaped (a status filter, no ids)
rather than a short enumerated list. An earlier draft of this case used
ids=[1,2,3], which is broad on 44c6f85 only because the ability NAME
contains a bulk token — exactly the derivation RFX-131 replaces with the
affected set. Under RFX-131 a 3-id delete is correctly `scoped`, the
contradiction does not arise, and `recoverable` is the right answer, so
the case tested nothing there. A predicate-selected set is broad under
both derivations (measured on 44c6f85 and on PR #94's head), which is
what makes this case portable across that change.
